title: Does This Photo from the Curiosity Rover Prove an Intense Sandstorm on Mars?
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementGeoscienceDoes This Photo from the Curiosity Rover Prove an Intense Sandstorm on Mars?Sand ripples preserved for billions of yearsDNBy David Nield11:15 AM CDT on July 24, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe Curiosity rover has been trundling over the red rocks and sand of Mars since August 2012, and it continues to make fascinating discoveries.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 1059.6K 10This Dinosaur’s Horns Are So Wild They Named It After a Marvel CharacterShareNextStayIn fact, it just uncovered evidence of a Martian sandstorm that lasted for hours and happened billions of years ago—the first direct physical evidence of such an event on the planet that we’ve found so far.What Curiosity spotted was ripples on ripples: Sand pushed so hard by the wind that the ripples are climbing over each other. These layers then hardened into rock over eons, leaving behind the geological patterns shown in this image, snapped by Curiosity on Dec. 12, 2024 in the Gale crater.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
